Client journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

01

Enquiry and first response

A prospective client contacts the firm through its website, a referral, email or WhatsApp. For law and CA firms this stage covers only replies to people who approach the firm; nothing here solicits work.

Touchpoints

  • Website enquiry form
  • Referral email from a client or another firm
  • WhatsApp message to the firm's business number
  • Call to the front desk or a partner

Accountable owner

Business development lead or intake partner

Automations on this stage

Enquiry and first response · 2–3 weeks

Enquiry capture, qualification and routing

Every new enquiry from forms, email, WhatsApp or referrals becomes one CRM record with a short AI summary, a suggested service line and a named owner, so prospects get a prompt and relevant reply.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Conflict, independence and KYC checks

Before any advice or work, the firm confirms it can act: no conflict with current or former clients, no threat to auditor independence, and client due diligence completed where the law requires it.

Touchpoints

  • Party, group company and director details
  • Conflict search against past matters
  • Independence review for audit clients
  • KYC and beneficial ownership documents

Accountable owner

Conflicts or risk partner

Automations on this stage

Conflict, independence and KYC checks · 5–8 weeks

Client acceptance: conflicts, independence and KYC

New clients and matters are checked against the firm's own records for conflicts, auditor independence and, where the law requires it, client due diligence, with every possible match and decision recorded before work starts.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Proposal and engagement terms

Scope, team, fee and terms are agreed in writing. Agencies and consultancies send proposals and statements of work; law and CA firms issue engagement letters.

Touchpoints

  • Scoping call notes
  • Proposal or statement of work
  • Engagement letter with fees and GST
  • E-signature

Accountable owner

Engagement partner

Automations on this stage

Proposal and engagement terms · 4–6 weeks

Proposals and engagement letters from approved libraries

Proposals, statements of work and engagement letters start from the firm's approved templates and rate card. AI drafts narrative sections only where the firm allows it, and a partner edits and approves every document before it goes for signature.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Onboarding and information gathering

The firm opens the matter or project, grants the right access and collects what it needs from the client: briefs and platform access for agencies, records and statements for CA firms.

Touchpoints

  • Kick-off call
  • Client brief form
  • Platform access requests
  • Secure document upload link
  • Shared channel or client portal

Accountable owner

Engagement manager or account lead

Automations on this stage

Onboarding and information gathering · 2–3 weeks

Agency client onboarding: access, brief and kick-off

When a statement of work is signed, the client gets one checklist for platform access, brand assets and the brief, and the team gets a ready project board, a shared channel and a kick-off agenda.

View the blueprint ↗Onboarding and information gathering · 4–6 weeks

Season-ready client document collection

For ITR, GST and audit work, each client gets a personalized checklist and a secure upload link, reminders follow an agreed schedule, and staff see in one tracker what is in, what is missing and what is ready for review.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Doing the work

Professionals draft, research, design and review. Automation prepares first drafts from approved templates, finds the firm's own precedents and keeps review rounds organized, while qualified people own the content.

Touchpoints

  • Drafts from approved templates
  • Precedent and knowledge search
  • Research notes with sources
  • Creative review rounds

Accountable owner

Matter lead, engagement manager or creative director

Automations on this stage

Doing the work · 2–4 weeks

Creative review, approval and claims check loop

Creative work moves through named review rounds in Figma or Canva with one place for feedback, a record of who approved which version, and a check that advertising claims have substantiation before launch.

View the blueprint ↗Doing the work · 4–6 weeks

Legal document assembly from the firm's templates

Legal notices, agreements, affidavits and routine applications are generated from approved templates and clause options using matter data, with every deviation highlighted for the drafting lawyer.

View the blueprint ↗Doing the work · 6–10 weeks

Knowledge assistant grounded in the firm's own work

Lawyers, CAs and consultants ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn only from the firm's approved precedents, opinions and past deliverables, with citations and matter-level access controls.

View the blueprint ↗Doing the work · 3–5 weeks

Research synthesis with traceable citations

Consultants get a structured research pack on a market, company or topic, built from permitted sources, with every statement linked to its source and gaps marked for an analyst to verify.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Dates, status and client updates

Hearing dates, statutory due dates, notice deadlines and project milestones are tracked in one place, and clients hear about progress before they need to ask.

Touchpoints

  • Hearing diary and cause lists
  • Client compliance calendar
  • Tax notice register
  • Weekly status report
  • Updates to clients who opted in

Accountable owner

Matter associate, compliance manager or account manager

Automations on this stage

Dates, status and client updates · 4–5 weeks

Client compliance calendar and tax notice tracker

One calendar holds every client's GST, TDS, advance tax, income tax and ROC due dates, plus any notices received, so staff get assigned tasks and clients get reminders for the services they have engaged.

View the blueprint ↗Dates, status and client updates · 2–4 weeks

Hearing diary, next-date updates and client reminders

After every hearing, the next date is recorded once and drives reminders for the advocate, the clerk and the brief preparation team, plus a short date-only update for clients who have opted in.

View the blueprint ↗Dates, status and client updates · 3–5 weeks

Weekly client status reports from delivery tools

Each week, work items from Jira or Asana, time logged and agreed campaign results are pulled into a draft status report that the account or engagement lead edits and sends.

View the blueprint ↗
07

Billing, collections and review

Time is captured daily, invoices go out with the right GST details, overdue fees are followed up courteously, and partners review utilization, realization and pipeline before the next cycle.

Touchpoints

  • Timesheets
  • Unbilled work report
  • GST invoice and payment link
  • Fee reminder
  • Partner dashboard

Accountable owner

Finance or billing lead with the engagement partner

Automations on this stage

Billing, collections and review · 3–5 weeks

Time capture, billing and fee reminders

Daily nudges keep timesheets current, unbilled work is visible every week, invoices are drafted with GST details for partner approval, and courteous reminders follow overdue fees.

View the blueprint ↗Billing, collections and review · 5–8 weeks

Utilization, realization and pipeline dashboard

Partners see one current view of staff utilization, realization against standard rates, unbilled work and weighted pipeline, built from timesheets, CRM and finance data with shared definitions.

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Enquiry capture, qualification and routingEnquiry and first responseThe partner or new-business lead reviews the summary, confirms or changes the qualification status, and decides whether to schedule a call, refer the prospect elsewhere or decline. The system never sends pricing or commits team capacity.
Client acceptance: conflicts, independence and KYCConflict, independence and KYC checksA designated conflicts partner in a law firm, or the engagement partner in a CA firm, reviews every possible match and decides. Any suspicion-related judgment under PMLA stays with the principal officer. The system never auto-clears a check, and nothing about a suspicion is shared with the client.
Proposals and engagement letters from approved librariesProposal and engagement termsThe engagement partner edits the draft, sets the final scope and fee, and approves it. Nothing reaches a client without that approval, and AI-drafted text stays highlighted until a person has reviewed it.
Agency client onboarding: access, brief and kick-offOnboarding and information gatheringThe account lead confirms that every access level follows least privilege, reviews the brief for gaps and approves the kick-off agenda. The client's own administrator grants each access.
Season-ready client document collectionOnboarding and information gatheringAn article or manager verifies each file against the checklist and marks it complete; the partner or signing CA reviews the prepared return or audit file. AI only labels documents. It never computes tax, files a return or decides what income is reportable.
Client compliance calendar and tax notice trackerDates, status and client updatesA manager changes the master calendar only after confirming an extension in the official CBIC, CBDT or MCA notification. Staff check extracted notice details against the original, and the partner decides the response strategy and signs every reply.
Hearing diary, next-date updates and client remindersDates, status and client updatesThe associate or clerk confirms each next date against the court's cause list or eCourts case status before saving it. Limitation and filing deadlines are calculated and entered by a lawyer, never by the system.
Weekly client status reports from delivery toolsDates, status and client updatesThe account or engagement lead edits the draft, confirms every number and decides which risks and decisions to raise. Nothing is sent to the client automatically.
Creative review, approval and claims check loopDoing the workThe creative director approves internal quality, the account lead resolves conflicting feedback, and only the client's named approver can give final sign-off. The client confirms substantiation for flagged claims before launch.
Legal document assembly from the firm's templatesDoing the workThe drafting lawyer reviews and edits every document, and a senior lawyer approves anything that leaves the firm. Lawyers decide clause choices and legal positions; the system only fills approved text.
Knowledge assistant grounded in the firm's own workDoing the workThe professional reads the cited sources before relying on anything and remains responsible for the advice. A named knowledge owner approves what is indexed and reviews flagged answers. The assistant never advises clients directly.
Research synthesis with traceable citationsDoing the workAn analyst checks every figure and quote against its source before use, and the engagement manager decides what goes into client material. Unverified items stay marked as unverified.
Time capture, billing and fee remindersBilling, collections and reviewThe engagement partner approves every invoice, write-down and write-off. The partner handles disputed fees and sensitive clients personally, and reminders stop as soon as an account is flagged.
Utilization, realization and pipeline dashboardBilling, collections and reviewPractice heads and the managing partner interpret the numbers and make staffing, pricing and hiring decisions. Definitions change only with their written approval, and no one's performance is judged from the dashboard alone.
